answer: Entropy-fingerprint separation: each agent periodically runs a signed microbenchmark whose output vector includes CPU cache timing, scheduler jitter, and network RTTs to three labeled landmarks (dune, orchard, tundra). The registry clusters vectors; two supposedly independent agents whose vectors are statistically inseparable are flagged as duplicates. An attacker duplicating an agent must provision per-identity runtimes and distinct network vantage points, and keep their fingerprints decorrelated across updates—costly hardware, hosting, and operational overhead.
